chosen.title: working from home with lower back pain
chosen.why: Pure side profile of a woman typing at a desk screen: shoulders rounded, chin pushed forward over the keyboard, so 'monitor + turtle neck' reads on the very first frame. 1.3-2.5s is the deepest, steadiest hunch; she only starts lifting off the keyboard at ~2.6s and grabs her lower back from 2.9s, so the cut ends just as the rise begins. Face is in profile only (no frontal), 16:9, natural window light, neutral white/grey palette that will grade down easily, no on-screen text or logos. Downsides: only 720p available; laptop rather than a desktop monitor, and a slightly staged stock look.

alternates.why: Best posture read of all (over-the-shoulder back view, rounded back, head forward at a desktop monitor, no face, 1080) BUT the file is 9:16 PORTRAIT (1080x1920); the strip tool stretches cells so it looked landscape. Usable only if a 1080x608 centre crop upscaled to 16:9 is acceptable, or in a split/pillarbox layout.

1080p 16:9 back-of-head view of a programmer hunched at a code monitor; no face. Heavy blue/teal grade, code text and a red toy on the desk, and the camera pans off the person after ~2.5s, so only 0-2.4s is usable.

notes: Mixkit's discover pages only exist for short tags, so the multi-word queries (office worker back view computer / hunched over computer / neck pain office / bad posture desk) returned nothing; 'tired office worker computer', 'neck pain', 'working late', 'back pain', 'programmer' and 'overtime' produced results (sheet budget was exceeded by a few because the first pick 39854 turned out to be portrait after download). 'neck pain' results were clinic/physio clips with no monitor and were skipped. Also downloaded and rejected: 24344 (720p, 3/4 frontal face at monitor) and 24063 (720p, frontal stretch). Files left in candidates/: s10_39854, s10_24344, s10_24063, s10_49479, s10_41637. Always verify orientation with ffprobe: the sheet/strip cells are force-resized and do not reveal aspect ratio.
